primary_collision_cause.explanation: Drivers turning left across oncoming traffic or turning on yellow without checking cross-traffic and crossing pedestrians.

behavior_factor.explanation: High-density commuter queues cause rear-end collisions when drivers follow too closely during rush hours.

for_drivers.details: Maintain at least 3 car lengths of space behind the vehicle ahead. Avoid tailgating near transit stops and expressway exit ramps where sudden stops occur.
for_drivers.key_tip: Leave 3-4 car lengths buffer on commercial transit corridors

for_pedestrians_and_cyclists.details: Make eye contact with drivers turning right on red before stepping into crosswalks. Use reflective gear or activate bicycle lights after dusk.
for_pedestrians_and_cyclists.key_tip: Never assume a turning driver has seen you at green lights

peak_danger_windows.secondary_peak: 10:00 PM - 2:00 AM Friday & Saturday (Reduced Lighting & Speed Variance)
peak_danger_windows.details: Evening rush hours experience 3x higher collision rates than midday. Exercise maximum patience during heavy congestion.
